To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) The equivalent circuit model for a DDS with internal losses is obtained by including a shunt conductive element in the cell and the manifold circuits; (b) The equivalent circuit of a cell can be modeled either with a series resistance or a shunt conductivity.

(1) a shunt conductive lossy cell model gives a better fit to the experimental data than a series resistive lossy cell; (2) the shunt conductive cell model is also a better fit to a lossy transmission line model for the cell; (3) the shunt model is more accurate for cells that have a high Q; and (4) the shunt lossy model gives the best fit to the experimental results for a structure with decoupled cells

(1) the inclusion of internal losses in the circuit model for the SLAC DDS does not significantly change the results obtained from the original lossless model; and (2) decoupling the cells at the ends from the manifols is an effective method to mitigate the performance degradation caused by the decoupling.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and analysis of a new type of accelerator structure, called the Damped Detuned Structure (DDS), that is intended for use in the SLC damping rings and in future damping rings for high-energy colliding-beams facilities.
the development and application of a circuit theory for the DDS which includes the effects of losses in the structure.
the design and analysis of damping structures for the damping of wakefields in the SLAC damping detuned structure (DDT).

a simple shunt conductance model is adequate to describe the damping effects in the manifolds and that the damping can be made sufficiently effective to mitigate performance degradation associated with cell decoupling.
